status: Test-only planning traces. Placeholder field names, not contract 0.1.0 and not the future P0-08 contract. Synthetic; no model output, no user data.

step_forms.event: apply a context event (see disclosure-model.ts Event)
step_forms.generate: snapshot an item at generation time from the current context (problem, version, attempt, revision, preference key, active request); optional show / queueVoice / cache
step_forms.present: check decide() for a previously generated item at this moment
step_forms.cache: cacheHit() for the active request; expect the id of the cached item it may reuse, or null
step_forms.surfaces: revalidate shown items and the voice queue after the preceding events; expect withdrawn/flushed ids
step_forms.expectPreferenceKey: the effective language/preference key of the current context

traces.note: The server accepted the offline request and it is still current, so the reconnect snapshot carries it. (Since the P0-12 QA follow-up, accepted means applied; the snapshot's request says what is current. See accepted-then-closed-by-another-device.)

covers: A43 (disclosure side only; entry linkage is not modeled)

traces.note: Lead-reported sequence (integration review of 4c32e49), extended with further snapshots.
Positive control: the user's own later explicit request is answered at its level; a stale snapshot does not replace it.
An offline close then an offline lower-level request that the server did not accept: the old full-solution snapshot must not come back.
Accepting the later offline request (still current in the snapshot) also acknowledges the earlier offline close; a newer server request then applies normally.
Returning to an attempt does not accept an older snapshot for it.
Liveness: once the server acknowledges the close (here in a resync while already connected), a causally later server request applies again.

AUDIO-14: a request heard in a late/backfilled transcript keeps its historical time and cannot open or escalate help, restore closed permission or resolve an unsynced close. The user's own later live request still works.

QA P012-D1 S1. A connected 'let me try' is pending until acknowledged; a reconnect at the version the device had before saying it cannot contain it. After the acknowledgement a later request applies, while the request 'let me try' cancelled never comes back (rule 7).

QA P012-D1 S1b and QA P012-D6 S4: newer snapshots without causal proof of the close (still carrying the old request, or a late request from another device) cannot reopen help until the close is acknowledged. After an acknowledgement, the model treats server order as causal (P012-D6, a P0-08 boundary; plan rule 11).

QA P012-D1 S1c. The user's own lower request is pending: a same-version reconnect or a newer snapshot without proof cannot bring back the older full solution. Once the server echoes the request, a later server request applies again.
QA P012-D2. The reconnect snapshot says the offline request was accepted (applied) but its current state is closed, e.g. 'let me try' on the iPhone ordered after it. Accepted is not current.

QA P012-D5 (a), liveness. An unsynced close, then the user's later connected request; the server echoing that request as current proves it has both intents, so a causally later iPhone request is shown.
QA H2. An older snapshot that arrives late is superseded together with its acknowledgement, and an acknowledgement for another attempt does not apply here.

QA P012-D5 (b). An offline close; the server acknowledges it while the user is on p2. After returning, help does not carry over, but a later server request for p1 applies without the acknowledgement being repeated.

An offline lower request that the server did not accept is no longer answered, but it still limits what the server may show until a later intent is acknowledged: the older full solution stays blocked, a lower server request may show.
ADR 0002 unknown order stays restrictive: a newer snapshot that does not contain the user's request may lower or close it, never widen it; the echo restores the server's authority.
Liveness. A reconnect at the version the device had when the user asked is known to be older than the request, so it neither answers nor restricts it.
A cached voice segment is never reused to answer a request; a cached card at the same binding is.

While the user is on p2, a newer p1 snapshot without the acknowledgement arrives first; an older p1 snapshot with it arrives late and is superseded, so the close still stands after returning. A new request after returning stays blocked too, because the close is still unacknowledged.

Review of 7ee1217: a reconnect at the version already applied is the same server state; its acknowledgement flags or accepted ids are not evidence, while the same acknowledgement in a newer snapshot is.
Review of 7ee1217: a lowered request stays pending through an equal-version reconnect that lists it as accepted; the older full solution stays out.

Review of 7ee1217 (safety-02): 'let me try', a request, then 'let me try' again. A close flag that accepts no request covers only the first run of closes, so a later other-device request stays blocked until the last close is acknowledged; the echoed request stays blocked for good (rule 7: the later close superseded it).

Review of 7ee1217 (A32): under the user's pending 'check step s1', a newer snapshot with an unscoped lower hint closes help rather than widening to the whole problem; after 'let me try' and a step check, a snapshot still carrying the closed hint changes nothing.
Review of 7ee1217: an offline step check that the server did not accept limits the server to that step: an unscoped goal hint stays out.
Review of 7ee1217: a connected 'let me try' never acknowledged, then an offline request the server does not accept: the close still blocks even a new request from another device.
Review of 7ee1217 (liveness): an offline request on p1, the user moves to p2 and reconnects there. The p1 request is dropped too, so later p1 server help at or below its level is shown on return.

Review of 7ee1217 (safety-06) and re-review of 8d67aaa: after a disconnection, a reconnect naming p2 says nothing about p1, so p1's other-device permission stays withdrawn until a p1 snapshot arrives; one at the version already recorded (nothing changed meanwhile) restores it.
Review of 7ee1217 (mutant A43): under the user's pending request, a lowered other-device request is withdrawn when a newer snapshot closes help.

Review of 7ee1217 (mutant A18): while on p2, a p1 acknowledgement at a version already recorded for p1 is not newer and does not resolve the close. A new request after returning stays blocked too, because the close is still unacknowledged.
Review of 7ee1217 (mutant A10): an acknowledgement for p1 delivered in a reconnect snapshot while on p2, after a disconnection, is kept.
Review of 7ee1217 (mutant A11): the same acknowledgement delivered in a reconnect snapshot while already connected is kept.

Review of 7ee1217 (mutants A01/A03), liveness: after an offline key-concept request is dropped at reconnect, a new server request at that level is shown at once; the request it superseded is not (rule 7).
QA P012-D8 / H6: a title cut from a full solution but labeled as a hint is never a cache answer for a hint request.
Liveness: the user asks while the server holds no request; after a brief disconnection, a reconnect at the same version (known to be older than the request) neither answers nor closes it.

Re-review of 8d67aaa (liveness): an offline request, then 'let me try', then a reconnect that acknowledges a close and accepts nothing. The only pending close is acknowledged (the request was received and not accepted), so a later other-device request is shown.

Re-review of 8d67aaa: a reconnect for another attempt withdraws other-device help on this attempt, but this device's own pending request stays answered, also after a newer snapshot that does not contain it and is higher.

Re-review of 8d67aaa: after a disconnection, a reconnect for this attempt at an older version than the device holds says nothing current; other-device help stays withdrawn until a snapshot at or above the recorded version.
Rule 7 per attempt: 'let me try' supersedes the full solution; after leaving and returning, an acknowledging snapshot that still names it does not bring it back.

Re-review of 8d67aaa: a snapshot for p1 received while away that is older than what the device recorded is not known (rule 7 does not retire its request); after returning, the user's own request is acknowledged and that request, current on the server, is shown.
